units.obligation: Stop the spread before diagnosing, and only look for the cause once the bleeding has stopped.

lessons.text:
Skipping this is the most common way a incident goes wrong.

Steps (3) and (4) of the triage order: stop the bleeding — pause the schedule or freeze the served partition — before diagnosing; only then look for cause. Freezing a wrong number in place is almost always better than letting it propagate while you think.
lessons.obligation: Stop the spread before diagnosing, and only look for the cause once the bleeding has stopped.

units.obligation: Structure the report to state the quantity, the reference, stratified agreement, failure cases and the domain of validity.

lessons.text:
The analyst owns this step.

Structure the validation as: definition of the quantity, reference data and why it is a fair reference, agreement statistics stratified by the dimensions that matter (season, geography, magnitude), failure cases shown rather than described, and a stated domain of validity. A validation that reports only pooled agreement hides exactly the regimes where the indicator fails.
lessons.anchor: 1. Validation report structure for a derived indicator
lessons.obligation: Structure the report to state the quantity, the reference, stratified agreement, failure cases and the domain of validity.

units.obligation: Report the sample size alongside any average, never the average alone.

lessons.text: Report the number of units, not just the mean. A mean reported without the number of units behind it invites over-reading a difference that the run-to-run variance, the paired comparison and the resampling test would not support.
lessons.obligation: Report the sample size alongside any average, never the average alone.

units.obligation: Keep the provenance record co-located with the output it describes.

lessons.text: Keep that record co-located with the artefact itself. An artefact whose origin cannot be reconstructed is not a deliverable. Nothing ships without lineage, and this section applies to every validation without exception.
lessons.obligation: Keep the provenance record co-located with the output it describes.

units.obligation: Track quality and coverage per derived value, exclude values failing the threshold, and label anything you filled in.

lessons.text:
Apply this before the validation leaves your hands.

A missing observation is not a zero. Track observation count and cloud fraction per derived value, drop scenes exceeding the cloud threshold, and label any gap-fill you perform. Coverage is a headline metric.
lessons.obligation: Track quality and coverage per derived value, exclude values failing the threshold, and label anything you filled in.

units.obligation: Assign a version number and write a changelog entry naming the behavioural difference before shipping.

lessons.text:
This section applies to every release without exception.

Gate the release on: validation signed by someone who did not build it, documentation
that a new user can follow unaided, a version number and a changelog entry that names
the behavioural difference, migration guidance for consumers of the previous version,
and a named owner for the first two weeks of questions.

The versioning half of the gate: "a version number and a changelog entry that names the behavioural difference". A changelog entry that does not name what behaves differently does not satisfy the gate.
lessons.anchor: 1. Indicator release readiness for this release
lessons.obligation: Assign a version number and write a changelog entry naming the behavioural difference before shipping.

units.obligation: Provide migration guidance for users of the previous version before releasing the new one.

lessons.text:
This section applies to every release without exception.

Gate the release on: validation signed by someone who did not build it, documentation
that a new user can follow unaided, a version number and a changelog entry that names
the behavioural difference, migration guidance for consumers of the previous version,
and a named owner for the first two weeks of questions.

The migration half of the gate: "migration guidance for consumers of the previous version". Consumers already on the old version must be told how to move.
lessons.anchor: 1. Indicator release readiness for this release
lessons.obligation: Provide migration guidance for users of the previous version before releasing the new one.

units.obligation: Name an owner who will field questions for the first two weeks after release.

lessons.text:
This section applies to every release without exception.

Gate the release on: validation signed by someone who did not build it, documentation
that a new user can follow unaided, a version number and a changelog entry that names
the behavioural difference, migration guidance for consumers of the previous version,
and a named owner for the first two weeks of questions.

The ownership half of the gate: "a named owner for the first two weeks of questions". The window is explicit — two weeks — and the owner is a named person, not a team or a rota.
lessons.anchor: 1. Indicator release readiness for this release
lessons.obligation: Name an owner who will field questions for the first two weeks after release.

units.obligation: Define the reversal path — the exact undo, its duration, its data loss — before touching a shared system.

lessons.text:
This section applies to every release without exception.

Define the reversal path before touching a shared system: the exact undo, its duration,
and its data loss. A backup-restore path counts only if the restore has been exercised.
Irreversible actions need a named approver and a scheduled slot.

All three parts are required before you touch the shared system: the exact undo, how long it takes, and what data it loses.
lessons.obligation: Define the reversal path — the exact undo, its duration, its data loss — before touching a shared system.

units.obligation: Exercise the restore before counting a backup as a valid reversal path.

lessons.text:
This section applies to every release without exception.

Define the reversal path before touching a shared system: the exact undo, its duration,
and its data loss. A backup-restore path counts only if the restore has been exercised.
Irreversible actions need a named approver and a scheduled slot.

"A backup-restore path counts only if the restore has been exercised." An untested restore is not a rollback plan.
lessons.obligation: Exercise the restore before counting a backup as a valid reversal path.

units.obligation: Add the checks at the same time as the thing they watch, not after the first incident.

lessons.text:
Apply this before the release leaves your hands.

Add the freshness, volume and null-rate checks at the same time as the pipeline, not
after the first incident. Alert on the user-visible symptom (stale or wrong data) rather
than on an internal proxy, and route every alert to a named owner with a runbook link.

The specific checks named are freshness, volume and null-rate, and they go in with the pipeline itself. Apply this before the release leaves your hands.
lessons.obligation: Add the checks at the same time as the thing they watch, not after the first incident.

units.obligation: Route every alert to a named owner and attach a link to its runbook.

lessons.text:
Apply this before the release leaves your hands.

Add the freshness, volume and null-rate checks at the same time as the pipeline, not
after the first incident. Alert on the user-visible symptom (stale or wrong data) rather
than on an internal proxy, and route every alert to a named owner with a runbook link.

Every alert needs both: a named owner it routes to, and a runbook link the owner can act on.
lessons.obligation: Route every alert to a named owner and attach a link to its runbook.

units.obligation: Add the new form alongside the old, move every reader across, and only then remove the old form.

lessons.text:
The data engineer owns this step.

Use expand-and-contract: add the new shape, dual-write, backfill, move readers across, verify equivalence on live traffic, and only then remove the old shape — with a gap of at least one full business cycle before the contract step.
lessons.obligation: Add the new form alongside the old, move every reader across, and only then remove the old form.

units.obligation: Never combine a change of structure with a change of meaning in one step; rename anything whose meaning changes.

lessons.text: Never combine a shape change and a semantic change in one migration; if a column's meaning changes, it gets a new name. The data engineer owns this step.
lessons.obligation: Never combine a change of structure with a change of meaning in one step; rename anything whose meaning changes.

units.obligation: List everyone who depends on the thing before you change it and give them the notice period you promised.

lessons.text: Enumerate downstream consumers before the change and give them the deprecation window you promised. This section applies to every migration without exception. Note what counts as breaking and therefore triggers the window: renaming, retyping, tightening nullability or changing units is breaking, even when the tests pass; adding an optional column is safe.
lessons.obligation: List everyone who depends on the thing before you change it and give them the notice period you promised.

units.obligation: Characterise a new source's real behaviour and limitations yourself before trusting it for any downstream work.

lessons.text:
Skipping this is the most common way a feed goes wrong.

Characterise the feed before trusting it: revisit interval and actual latency distribution (not the advertised one), native resolution and resampling behaviour, radiometric calibration and known artefacts, the vendor's own quality flags, and their restatement policy.
lessons.obligation: Characterise a new source's real behaviour and limitations yourself before trusting it for any downstream work.

units.obligation: Run the new source in parallel with the incumbent and quantify the difference before switching over.

lessons.text: Run a parallel period against the incumbent source and quantify the level shift before any switchover. Skipping this is the most common way a feed goes wrong — a silent level shift between the old and new source is otherwise discovered only after the switch.
lessons.obligation: Run the new source in parallel with the incumbent and quantify the difference before switching over.

units.obligation: Share aggregates only, and use identifiers that cannot be re-linked to individuals or clients.

lessons.text: Share aggregates, and use identifiers that cannot be re-linked. Personal data and client-identifying detail stay out of shared repos, tickets, logs and notebooks, so anything that leaves must be aggregated and keyed on identifiers with no path back to the original subject.
lessons.anchor: 2. Keep personal and client-confidential data out for this feed
lessons.obligation: Share aggregates only, and use identifiers that cannot be re-linked to individuals or clients.

units.obligation: Attach a record of origin to every output and keep it beside the artefact.

lessons.text:
Skipping this is the most common way a feed goes wrong.

Attach a lineage record to every output: input dataset versions, coverage window, code revision, config hash. Co-locate it with the artefact so the two cannot drift apart.

If you cannot satisfy this, stop and escalate.
lessons.obligation: Attach a record of origin to every output and keep it beside the artefact.

units.obligation: Use half-open intervals consistently across every place a range appears, and record the convention explicitly.

lessons.text:
Apply this before the feed leaves your hands.

Use half-open intervals [start, end) consistently across filenames, partitions, queries and API calls, and record the convention explicitly.

If you cannot satisfy this, stop and escalate.
lessons.obligation: Use half-open intervals consistently across every place a range appears, and record the convention explicitly.

units.obligation: Hand-check the first and last boundary of a range against the job's actual output.

lessons.text: Hand-check the first and last partition against the job's output; boundary errors dominate temporal bugs. This is the check on the half-open [start, end) convention actually holding across filenames, partitions, queries and API calls. If you cannot satisfy this, stop and escalate.
lessons.obligation: Hand-check the first and last boundary of a range against the job's actual output.

units.obligation: Distinguish a missing observation from an observed zero, and carry the counts that prove which.

lessons.text:
This section applies to every feed without exception.

Separate absence of signal from absence of observation: carry per-value counts and cloud fraction, apply the cloud threshold, flag interpolated points.

If you cannot satisfy this, stop and escalate.
lessons.anchor: 8. Handle cloud cover and missing observations
lessons.obligation: Distinguish a missing observation from an observed zero, and carry the counts that prove which.

units.obligation: Publish coverage and completeness prominently alongside the results rather than burying them.

lessons.text: Publish coverage prominently. This section applies to every feed without exception: a value that is low because nothing was observed must be distinguishable by the reader from a value that is low because the signal was low, which is why per-value counts, cloud fraction and interpolation flags travel with the output. If you cannot satisfy this, stop and escalate.
lessons.anchor: 8. Handle cloud cover and missing observations
lessons.obligation: Publish coverage and completeness prominently alongside the results rather than burying them.

units.obligation: Confine locale-specific formatting to the presentation layer alone, never to stored or exchanged data.

lessons.text: Local formats belong to the presentation layer alone. Storage is SI, EPSG:4326 for coordinates, equal-area for area maths, UTC for time. If you cannot satisfy this, stop and escalate.
lessons.anchor: 9. Be explicit about units, CRS and time zones for this feed
lessons.obligation: Confine locale-specific formatting to the presentation layer alone, never to stored or exchanged data.
